editorial_examples.note: The candidate’s “American double continent” is not idiomatic English; the replacement uses the natural English name for the landmass.

editorial_examples.german: Der Staatsanwalt kann nicht beweisen, dass es niemand anderes getan hat.
editorial_examples.english: The prosecutor cannot prove that nobody else did it.
editorial_examples.note: The candidate English double negation changes the logical reading of the German; the revised translation preserves it.

editorial_examples.german: Verzeihen Sie die Störung, aber da ist ein Anruf für Sie.
editorial_examples.english: Excuse the interruption, but there is a call for you.
editorial_examples.note: The candidate translates the German noun Störung as an English verb; the replacement preserves the noun sense more directly.

editorial_examples.german: Wir können ihn nicht freilassen; die Gefahr, dass er wieder mordet, ist zu hoch.
editorial_examples.english: We cannot release him; the risk that he will murder again is too high.
editorial_examples.note: The candidate weakens morden to the broader verb kill; the revised translation retains the specific meaning murder.

editorial_examples.german: Die befreiten Geiseln wurden medizinisch untersucht.
editorial_examples.english: The freed hostages received medical examinations.
editorial_examples.note: The candidate uses befreit as a finite verb, while this entry is labeled adjective; the replacement uses the participial adjective attributively.
